newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares close near high despite Ciba, Sandoz.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares close near high despite Ciba, Sandoz.

text.p: 1540 GMT - Swiss shares closed near the day's high after a friendly Wall Street opening lifted the blue-chip Swiss Market Index above resistance around 3,875 points, offsetting downside pressure stemming from a fall in Ciba and Sandoz.
Ciba and Sandoz, which on Wednesday won final approval to merge into Novartis, slumped more than one percent each on profit-taking and switches from shares into convertible bonds.
Also, some funds may be selling Ciba and Sandoz since Novartis will have a weighting of 26 percent in the SMI, and the funds would be invested too heavily in one stock, dealers said.
* The SMI added 6.8 points, or 0.18 percent, to 3,880.8.
* All share SPI closed up 4.14 points, or 0.17 percent, to 2,475.76 points.

Dealers said the prospects for the bourse were ideal, citing a firming U.S. dollar and low interest rates. The expiry of the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) on Friday did not influence the market much.
* Roche certificates profited from Ciba's and Sandoz's weakness. Roche firmed 120 francs to 10,190 while Ciba registereds fell 19 francs to 1,604 and Sandoz plummeted 23 francs to 1,502.
* Rollover transactions ahead of Friday's expiry dominated trade on Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex).

SMI futures were lifted up by short covering. Of a total of 15,093 SMI contracts traded, 8,719 were December SMI futures and 6,326 January SMI futures. December SMI futures rose 15.5 points to 3,891.0 points.

UBS, Novartis, Nestle and to some extent Winterthur saw lively demand among options. The total options volume reached 154,827 contracts with a call put ratio of 1.37 to one. 29,518 SMI options were traded.
* ABB, Surveillance and SMH were up more than one percent, profiting from the easing tendency in the Swiss franc.
* Among financials, CS Holding , UBS bearer shares, SBC and Baloise gained between 0.7 to 0.9 percent.
* Swissair slumped 5.7 percent to 1,025 francs. Dealers said the share moves have been volatile in recent times.
Some investors, which expected "something spectacular" from Thursday's press conference, were disappointed with Swissair's announcement of a reorganisation and took profits, dealers said.
